summary: Cowlitz County, WA lookout on Powder Horn Peak: L-4 cab (1930 or 1931), smokehouse tower, 1960 DNR live-in tower; discontinued 1969 and listed as gone.

facts.design: L-4 cab, then a two-story smokehouse-type tower, then a 20-foot wooden DNR live-in tower (1960)
facts.status_note: Firetower.org says it is now gone and the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the tower as gone; no source describes what remains at the site

visit.drive_up: Off Highway 503 not far from I-5, per WillhiteWeb
visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb describes a low mountain with a rocky summit that should offer views, reached from Highway 503 not far from I-5 and called a quick bonus peak; it describes no structure on the summit today

events.note: L-4 cab; a 1930 newspaper says it was in use by August 1930, while firetower.org and firelookout.com date it to 1931
Edward McGrill named as lookout when the new lookout went into use
Two-story smokehouse-type tower with enlarged living quarters; firetower.org says the 1940s
I.G. Driver manned the station the previous summer, with his dog as his only companion
I.G. Driver assigned again in June 1954
20-foot wooden DNR live-in tower replaced the smokehouse
Discontinued because of air patrols, per The Oregonian (August 18, 1969); the same item says it would most likely be burned, a forecast only
Planned move to the Clark College campus in Vancouver as an exhibit; the project never happened
Photo captioned Equipment on site, dated 7/24/2000; the latest dated on-site detail found
Registered February 11, 2011 as FFLOS US 843, WA 44

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com date the L-4 cab to 1931; a 1930 newspaper clip says it was in use by August 1930, and WillhiteWeb gives 1930. The story gives 1930 as first use and notes the 1931 dates.
firelookout.com says 10 miles northeast of Woodland; the 1969 Oregonian clip says about nine. The story says roughly nine to ten.

The 1969 Oregonian clip reports discontinuation, while firelookout.com lists the tower years as 1960-1970. The story uses 1969 for discontinuation and treats 1970 as the date of the planned exhibit move.
firetower.org says the smokehouse came in the 1940s; the 1947 state report and WillhiteWeb say 1947. The story uses the 1940s and cites the 1947 report.
WillhiteWeb titles this site Davis Peak, while the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a separate ground site named Davis Peak near Cle Elum. The story keeps them apart.

notes_for_editor: Access level left unset: no source names the landowner or says whether the summit is open, so the Highway 503 route appears only in visit. other_names 'Davis Mountain' is not tied to this site in any page read; WillhiteWeb uses Davis Peak for this site instead. Brief source 6 (trail_202) is a different Davis Peak near Cle Elum and is corrected. The 1969 Oregonian item predicts a burn but no source confirms one or dates the tower's removal. The Weebly page closes its entry with the word Removed and no date. No photos recorded: no image URLs were available in the cached text.
